question: Should Android Installed Apps be disabled for legacy opt-ins until the user accepts this disclosure version, and should the new Data Safety upload lane become part of the Play release process?
rationale: The code fix is plausible, but the upgrade reset and Google Play/privacy rollout are maintainer-owned decisions outside what source inspection can safely approve.

options.title: Accept reset and rollout
options.body: Resolve the merge conflict, keep the consent-version reset, and merge after confirming Play Console, privacy-policy, and review materials.

options.title: Adjust disclosure first
options.body: Revise the wording, placement, or legacy migration policy, then repeat the emulator proof before merge.

options.title: Pause for release materials
options.body: Hold the branch until the Data Safety CSV, Play Console state, and privacy-policy update are ready to ship together.

recommendation.title: Accept reset and rollout
recommendation.body: Resolve the merge conflict, keep the consent-version reset, and merge after confirming Play Console, privacy-policy, and review materials.

likelyOwner.reason: CONTRIBUTING.md routes the Android app to obviyus, and the related installed-apps feature was merged through that account.
